newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Dec 20.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Dec 20.

text.p: Nine main Mexican ports were closed to shipping Friday including the country's three crucial crude ports, sources said Friday.

Port officials told Reuters at least two crude ports could reopen later today. The three Gulf of Mexico ports were closed Wednesday as a cold front hit the area causing wind velocities of up to 80 km per hour and waves up to 16 feet high.

Officials at Pajaritos port in Veracruz state said wind speeds had relaxed and they were deciding whether to reopen the port. Dos Bocas officials in Tabasco state said winds were at between 20 to 30 kilometers per hour, about half Thursday's speeds. They were also considering reopening.
The largest crude shipping port, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, was still experiencing strong winds and dangerously high waves, officials said.

Tuxpan, Coatzacoalcos, Frontera, Ciudad del Carmen, Campeche and Progreso were named as the six other ports still not allowing outgoing movements, the Communications and Trasportation Ministry said in its daily update.

Minor ports also closed were Nautla and Alvarado. Closed to small vessels, namely fishing and tourist vessels, were the ports of La Paz, Loreto, Santa Rosalia, Cozumel, Puerto Juarez, Salina Cruz, the ministry added.
The ministry updated weather and shipping conditions for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.
Moderate rains along the coast of Jalisco, Colima, Michoacan, Guerrero, Oaxaca. Winds from the northeast of 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 kilometers/11 to 17 miles per hour).

Cold front bringing moderate rains and low temperatures with isolated squalls along the coost. Winds from the north and northeast at 20 to 25 knots and gusts of 30 knots. Waves up to 10 feet, although decreasing during the day.
Cold front also affecting Caribbean, bringing clodier than usual weather and light rains on the coast of Quintana Roo state. Winds from the north at 10 to 15 knots with waves up to 10 feet high.
